Synopsis:
Voss waits in the sewers until you get the hammer. Then he's there with the dragon he rode in Act1 in humanoid form. If you show him the hammer then, he rewards you with a Silver Sword and then leaves to meet you in endgame.He will still be in endgame even if you didn't do this step, but you just would have missed on the Silver Sword.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_VossSewers.json: Late‑game, at the “point of no return” before the Netherbrain, Kith’rak Voss turns up in the sewers (his dragon mount now in humanoid form) waiting for you to retrieve the Orphic Hammer. If you show him the hammer there he will reward you with a Silver Sword and then depart to meet you again in the endgame; if you never presented it, he still appears later but the sword is lost. Voss is a furious Githyanki who served Prince Orpheus and wants the hammer to break Orpheus’s chains—his tone and willingness to help depend on whether Orpheus is alive, dead, or transformed. Lae’zel and other companions may be present; Voss references leads (a diabolist named Raphael and the House of Hope) and the continuing watch of his honour guard when urging you to find the hammer.
- END_GameFinale_RaphaelCrownUpdate.json: After WithersChronicles, if the player made the deal with Raphael (the Orphic Hammer in exchange for the Crown of Karsus), Raphael shows up to report back on how that went.
- CAMP_Orthon_DiabolistHint.json: Orthon Yurgir appears in camp to help you after players helped him, telling about Orphic Hammer in House of Hope
- END_IllithidOptions_RaphaelLastChance.json: The player has burned their bridges. They attacked the Emperor, causing him to leave the Astral Prism as a foe, and they have no hammer to free Orpheus, as they need his protection against the influence of the Netherbrain. After a short pause to let the players feel the weight of their actions, Raphael appears before them, with a new deal: accept the hammer from Raphael, freeing Orpheus in exchange for giving him the Crown. At this point, the player has no other option except for a game over.
- GLO_Laezel_WRD_LearnedAboutOrphicHammer.json: Laezel wants to talk about the Orphic hammer and how the players must get it in order to free/kill Orpheus.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Kith'rak Voss: Have you brought the Orphic Hammer? (node 6)
- Kith'rak Voss: Have you retrieved the Orphic Hammer? Will our prince's chains finally be broken? (node 5)
- Player: Any idea where I might find the Hammer? (node 23)
- Kith'rak Voss: A devil of Raphael's stature does not simply make camp on the shores of the Styx. (node 53)
- Kith'rak Voss: He will have made a sanctuary for himself. A lavish one, too, one that caters to his many vices. (node 64)
- Lae'zel: The House of Hope. We must find a way in. (node 17)
- Kith'rak Voss: He must keep the Orphic Hammer there. (node 11)
- Kith'rak Voss: Every house has an entrance, istik - even those in the Hells. A diabolist in this very city might know the way. || [context] NodeContext: vin-ISK / ISS-tik (node 61)

Sample 2:
- Kith'rak Voss: Have you brought the Orphic Hammer? (node 6)
- Kith'rak Voss: Have you retrieved the Orphic Hammer? Will our prince's chains finally be broken? (node 5)
- Player: Where are the rest of your allies? (node 38)
- Kith'rak Voss: The remaining honour guard serve as my eyes and ears. (node 7)
- Kith'rak Voss: Vlaakith's forces hunt you and the Prism. My allies have slayed more than you know, so that you might travel freely. (node 18)
- Kith'rak Voss: As for those that break through, you've proven more than capable of bleeding them yourself. (node 63)

Sample 3:
- Kith'rak Voss: Have you brought the Orphic Hammer? (node 6)

- Player: I haven't recovered the Hammer just yet. (node 43)
- Kith'rak Voss: Then I will wait here until you have. The chains that bind Orpheus also bind the whole of the githyanki people. (node 40)

context: Late in the game, at the point of no return before the Netherbrain, Kith’rak Voss turns up in the sewers (his dragon mount now in humanoid form) waiting for you to retrieve the Orphic Hammer. If you show him the hammer there he rewards you with a Silver Sword and then departs to meet you again in the endgame; if you never present it, he still appears later but the sword is lost. Voss is a furious Githyanki who served Prince Orpheus and wants the hammer to break Orpheus’s chains, and his tone and willingness to help depend on whether Orpheus is alive, dead, or transformed. He mentions leads — the diabolist Raphael and the House of Hope — and the continuing watch of his honour guard; companions such as Lae’zel may be present and push you toward those leads. Certain late-game choices (for example deals with Raphael or burned bridges) can change how or whether you gain access to the hammer.
